leads.name: Zomereik (Pedunculate Oak)
leads.place: Ambeltpad, Veldhoek (wijk Berkum, Stadsdeel Oost), Zwolle
leads.reason: The register's own site_history says this specific oak was planted in 1911 on an old levee (oeverwal) of the Overijsselse Vecht, which is a genuinely good story. But the municipality's own 2024 special-trees list (CVDR757712) shows Ambeltpad lined with dozens of near-identical Quercus robur / ZOMEREIK entries, most planted 1930-1931, classified 'Monumentaal Particulier' with no individual names or landmarks distinguishing one from another, the same avenue pattern that got the Philosofenallee oak (register nr 1683416) blocked earlier. This one's 1911 planting date is a decade older than most of its neighbours, which could make it distinguishable, but nothing found this pass names or photographs THIS specific tree apart from the row. Needs either a source that singles it out (an address number, a photo, a local write-up) or a site visit before it can ship as a collectible point rather than one of an avenue.

leads.name: Zomereik (Pedunculate Oak)
leads.place: "Nu nog weiland" (still meadow for now), Zwolle
leads.reason: No age at all, register reason is 'potentieel' (candidate for future designation, the lowest tier seen in this register for Zwolle), owner_category unknown, and the place name itself ('still meadow for now') suggests the site may be slated for development rather than being an established, findable spot. No address, no second source found. Too thin to research further within this pass's budget; a future pass with more time could try to place it precisely and check ownership/access.

leads.name: The Plume Elm of Potgietersingel
leads.species: Elm (Ulmus sp., a plume-form cultivar; possibly Ulmus x hollandica)
leads.age_estimate: roughly 130 years, from a registered planting date around 1900
leads.story: The Plume Elm of Potgietersingel does not appear on Zwolle's own list of protected trees. The municipality's 2015 survey of the city's special trees names nineteen elms across town and catalogues the rest of this exact park strip in detail, its maples, oaks, planes and even a tree of heaven, and still skips this one. The only record of it at all is the national Landelijk Register Monumentale Bomen, which dates the planting to around 1900 and calls it a Pluimiep, Dutch for plume elm, after its narrow, weeping crown. The register is not settled on what species it actually is: one entry names Ulmus x hollandica, a duplicate entry backs off to Ulmus sp. Dutch elm disease has killed most of the country's old elms since the 1970s, which makes a plume-form specimen from around 1900 still standing, in a public strip the city owns and leaves open at all hours, worth more attention than its own municipality has given it. It stands about a hundred and twenty metres from the park's Copper Beech, part of the same walk. Nobody has settled the exact cultivar, and the page would welcome someone who can.
leads.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the narrow, plume-shaped crown, unlike the broader elms elsewhere in the city. It stands in the park strip at Potgietersingel, about 120 metres from the Copper Beech by the Fountain.
verified_sources: Landelijk Register Monumentale Bomen (Bomenstichting), register nr 1689103
leads.access: Free. Stands in the public park strip at Potgietersingel (gemeente-owned), open at any time; about 120m from the Copper Beech by the Fountain (zwo_006), so it joins that same walk.
leads.transport: About 700 m north of Zwolle station, same stop as the Van Nahuysplein cluster.
leads.removed_reason: Dead or felled per the register itself: Landelijk Register Monumentale Bomen nr 1689103 carries status 5, Dood/geveld (checked 2026-10-10 against the Bomenstichting ArcGIS layer). Inspector remark: "schouw 9 juli 1996. Op de entplaats gemeten. Niet meer aanwezig? 3 feb 2007. Bij laatste schouw Niet gevonden 09-12-2011, JD" Removed under the rule that a dead tree is never a collectible entry.

leads.name: The Horse Chestnut of the Park Eekhout
leads.age_estimate: roughly 165 to 175 years, from the register's planting band of 1850 to 1860
leads.story:
A horse chestnut that has reached a hundred and seventy years is doing better than most of its kind manage now.

The species has had a bad half century in Europe. Bleeding canker, a bacterial infection that leaves rusty weeping patches on the bark, has killed a large share of mature trees since the 1990s. The horse chestnut leaf miner, a moth whose larvae tunnel between the leaf surfaces, arrived in the Netherlands around 2002 and now browns the foliage of nearly every tree in the country from July onward. The moth does not kill, but a tree that loses its leaves two months early every year for twenty years is a weakened tree.

So an old, big, still standing chestnut is worth registering as the survivor it is.

It stands in the southeast part of the Park Eekhout, on the ring of the old fortifications, banded 1850 to 1860.

Come in the first half of May, before the miner gets going. That is when the tree does the thing it was planted for: hundreds of upright white flower spikes over the whole crown, each one with a yellow throat that turns red once the flower has been pollinated and no longer wants visitors.
leads.access: Free. Public park, open at any time.
leads.transport: About 900 m northwest of Zwolle station, in the Park Eekhout.
leads.how_to_recognise: Big palmate leaves in fans of five to seven leaflets, in the southeast part of the park.

best_time.label: early May, when the white candles are up and the throats are still yellow

leads.removed_reason: Landelijk Register Monumentale Bomen carries the matched entries (1689105, 1683412, 1689576, 1688386) as status 5, Dood/geveld

leads.name: The Beech of Ter Pelkwijkpark
leads.age_estimate: disputed: register says roughly 140 years, the municipality's 2024 list says roughly 95 years
leads.access: Free. Public park (Ter Pelkwijkpark), owned by the municipality, open to all.
leads.transport: About 1.3 km northeast of Zwolle station, roughly 15 minutes on foot.
leads.story:
Two official bodies have dated this beech and they are fifty years apart.

The national register of monumental trees puts the planting between 1880 and 1890. Zwolle's own 2024 list of special trees, describing the same species in the same park under the same municipal ownership and the same monumental status, says 1930. Neither is a guess by us and neither gets dismissed here. Both are the work of people who went and looked, decades apart, and the honest answer is that this tree is somewhere between about 95 and 145 years old.

The gap changes what it lived through. On the register's dating it was already a substantial tree when German troops entered Zwolle in May 1940. On the municipality's it was a ten year old sapling that grew up through the occupation and the Canadian liberation of the city in April 1945.

What is not in dispute is that it is the odd one out. Ter Pelkwijkpark is an oak park: more than a dozen pedunculate oaks carry register entries here, a dense municipal stand of one species. This beech is the only one of its kind among them, which makes it the easiest tree in the park to find and the hardest to date.

If anyone has a girth measurement, it would settle the argument.
leads.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the only beech in a park of oaks: smooth grey bark instead of furrowed, and oval leaves with wavy edges rather than lobes. It stands among the dozen registered pedunculate oaks of Ter Pelkwijkpark.

best_time.label: late October into November, when it turns copper and russet

leads.removed_reason: Landelijk Register Monumentale Bomen carries the matched entries (1689105, 1683412, 1689576, 1688386) as status 5, Dood/geveld

leads.name: The Plane of the Badhuiswal
leads.age_estimate: disputed: register says roughly 160 years, the municipality's 2024 list says roughly 75 years

location.address: Badhuiswal, next to the former Party restaurant Zizi, Zwolle

leads.access: Free. Stands on the public Badhuiswal, owned by the municipality.
leads.transport: About 1.6 km north of Zwolle station, roughly 19 minutes on foot.
leads.story:
This plane is either about 160 years old or about 75, and the two official sources may not be describing the same tree at all.

The national register carries a gewone plataan on the Badhuiswal planted between 1860 and 1870, owned by the municipality, rated monumental. Zwolle's own 2024 list carries a plane on the Badhuiswal planted in 1950, owned by the municipality, rated a tier lower at waardevol. Same street, same owner, same species, ninety years of daylight between them. The Badhuiswal is a short quay and it holds several registered planes and oaks, so the likeliest reading is that two surveys walked past two different trees.

The dating decides what it has seen. On the earlier one it went in while Zwolle was pulling down its old defences and rebuilding the ground as a ring of water and planting, and it has stood on this quay through every war since. On the later one it is a postwar tree, planted into a city five years out of occupation.

Girth would settle it in about a minute, because a plane of 160 years and a plane of 75 are not remotely the same size, and nobody has published a measurement for this one. If you walk past with a tape, tell us what it says.
leads.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the bark, flaking off in cream and olive plates like camouflage, and by the bristly seed balls that hang on all winter. It stands on the Badhuiswal beside the building that was Party restaurant Zizi.
leads.removed_reason: Landelijk Register Monumentale Bomen carries the matched entries (1689105, 1683412, 1689576, 1688386) as status 5, Dood/geveld

leads.name: The Copper Beech by Restaurant Urbana
leads.age_estimate: disputed and species detail uncertain: register says roughly 160 years, the municipality's 2024 list may describe a different, younger private beech on the same street

location.address: Wipstrikkerallee 213, in front of the former restaurant Urbana (now Loetje), Zwolle

leads.access: Privately owned grounds; visitability and visibility are unrecorded ('onbekend') in the national register. Given it stands in front of the same restaurant building as zwo_013, it is plausible it is street-visible, but this is not confirmed.
leads.transport: About 2.3 km southwest of Zwolle station, roughly 27 minutes on foot; a bus or short bike ride is quicker.
leads.story:
The national register lists this beech, gives it monumental status, and then leaves two boxes blank. Can you visit it: unknown. Can you see it: unknown.

What the entry does say is specific. A bruine beuk, a copper beech rather than a plain one, on private ground at the Wipstrikkerallee, planted between 1860 and 1870. That dating would make it a grown tree well before Villa Urbana opened as a tea house next door in 1924, and by some distance the oldest thing at this corner of the avenue.

The corroboration is thinner than we would like. Zwolle's 2024 list of special trees records no copper beech on this street at all. It does record a private plain beech here, dated 1940, which is either the same tree written up loosely by a different surveyor or an entirely different one, and the avenue holds more than a dozen registered beeches, so either is possible. The age therefore sits in a wide band, somewhere between about 85 and 165 years.

Both questions come apart with one visit. Purple leaves mean the register has it right, green leaves mean it does not, and either way you will know whether you can stand in front of it. Tell us which.
leads.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the purple foliage, which is what separates it from the plain green beeches further along the avenue. It stands in front of the former Urbana tea house, now Loetje, with the big plane beside the building.
leads.removed_reason: Landelijk Register Monumentale Bomen carries the matched entries (1689105, 1683412, 1689576, 1688386) as status 5, Dood/geveld

blocked.name: Zomereik (Pedunculate Oak)
blocked.place: Weiland naast Huis den Doorn, Den Doornweg 47, Genne
blocked.reason_blocked: DEAD. The register's own site_history for the neighbouring oak at the same address (nr 1688462, also blocked, below) states in its own words that in the storm of 18 January 2007 'deze eik net als de naburige kleinere eik nr 1689611 ontworteld' (this oak, like the neighbouring smaller oak nr 1689611, was uprooted). The register carries no vitality field and does not flag nr 1689611 itself as dead, but its sibling entry's text names it explicitly as felled in the same storm. Never ship; a tree we know is dead never goes live.

blocked.name: Zomereik (Pedunculate Oak)
blocked.place: In weiland, zuid kant huis Den Doorn, Den Doornweg 47, Genne
blocked.reason_blocked: DEAD. The register's own site_history for this entry is unusually detailed and self-documenting: it was one of the ten thickest oaks in the Netherlands at 682cm circumference, but 'Bij de zware storm van 18 januari 2007 is deze eik... ontworteld. Het wortelstelsel bleek aangetast en de boom was onderin hol' (in the storm of 18 January 2007 this oak was uprooted; the root system was found to be damaged and the trunk was hollow at the base). The same text gives a ring count from the exposed cross-section (173 rings, oak estimated 180-190 years old, planted around 1820-1830) which is itself now historical rather than current. Never ship a tree known to be dead. Also note this and nr 1689611 above are both on private agricultural land (owner_category particulier, setting agrarisch) roughly 4.7 km outside central Zwolle in the hamlet of Genne, which would also have needed an access check even if alive.
